--- title: "BWM LFP Release QC: Survival-Floor Fix Validation" description: "Quality-control report for the v03 Brain-Wide Map LFP release: validates the survival-floor fix against the live dataset and summarises release-wide RMSE, compression ratio, and saturation." date: "2026-07-24" author: "Olivier Winter" categories: [electrophysiology, LFP, compression, Neuropixels, quality-control] --- ## Overview This is the release-QC companion to the [SVD/WP compression benchmark](index.qmd): where that page derives and calibrates the codec, this one validates the actual shipped **v03 Brain-Wide Map (BWM) release** — 699 recordings, both the default (ε=150, α=28) and aggressive (ε=450, α=96) compression passes — against the dataset it replaces on S3 (referred to here as **v00**). Three things are checked: 1. **The survival-floor fix** (`floor_k=64`, see [index.qmd §Adaptive WP threshold calibration](index.qmd#adaptive-wp-threshold-calibration)) actually eliminates the zero-damage failure mode in the shipped data, with no regressions. 2. **Saturation detection and muting** — an entirely new pipeline stage in v03, absent from v00 — is present and correctly labelled across the release. 3. **Release-wide RMSE / CR** fall in the expected range across all 699 recordings, not just the 11 benchmark PIDs used to calibrate ε/α. ## Zero-damage fix: v00 vs v03 Before the fix, low-SNR chunks could be over-thresholded at the wavelet-packet stage until *every* coefficient of the dominant SVD row was discarded, reconstructing to exact zero — silently destroying real (if weak) LFP. The root cause and fix are detailed in [index.qmd](index.qmd#adaptive-wp-threshold-calibration); this section confirms it holds at release scale. **Method.** A chunk decompresses to exact zero iff every coefficient of `Vh_hat` was thresholded away, which is visible directly from the stored `vh_indices` dataset length — no decompression needed. For each of the 699 BWM recordings, in both the live (v00) and new (v03) archive, the zero-time fraction was computed as `Σ(chunk length where n_kept==0) / Σ(chunk length)`. ::: {#84cdc4fb .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
pass overall zero-time (v00) overall zero-time (v03) recordings affected (v00) recordings affected (v03) regressions (v03 worse)
0 default 0.92% 0.00% 36 0 0
1 aggressive 3.79% 0.00% 148 0 0
``` ::: ::: Zero-time-fraction dropped to **exactly 0.00%** across all 699 recordings in both passes, with **zero regressions** — no recording is worse in v03 than in v00. The worst pre-fix offenders (up to 99.8% zero-time in the default pass, i.e. essentially the entire recording silently discarded) are now fully recovered: ![Survival-floor fix: the 15 recordings with the highest pre-fix zero-time fraction, before (v00) and after (v03), both compression passes. Every v03 bar is exactly zero.](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_zero_damage_before_after.png){.lightbox} Two recordings (`4037a618…`, `46630957…`) are **not** part of this fix: both have `frac_bad = 1.0` (all 384 channels flagged bad by bad-channel detection) and were never zero-time in *either* version — a distinct, expected failure mode (dead/noisy input, not over-thresholding) already tracked separately in `qc_fully_bad_recordings.csv`. They are flagged for exclusion from downstream analysis, not for recompression. ## Saturation detection & muting — new in v03 v00 ships **no saturation information at all** — the `//saturation` HDF5 group doesn't exist anywhere in the live archive. v03 adds a full insertion-level saturation pipeline: ADC-clipped spans are detected on the raw LFP band (before any filtering, so pre-processing can't obscure the clipping), recorded as a per-recording interval table, and **muted** — zeroed with a cosine taper — on the decimated output *after* Cadzow denoising. This "late" re-mute was chosen over an early, pre-filter mute in a 2026-07-21 A/B comparison: muting the raw traces before the highpass/CAR/decimate/Cadzow chain did not keep the span clean — those stages leaked residual energy (and spurious CSD sources/sinks) back into it — so a single re-mute of the final output is both cleaner and cheaper. ::: {#6081c985 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
pass recordings with saturation mean saturated fraction total saturated time total saturated intervals correctly labelled muted=True
0 default 446 / 699 0.98% 9.2 h 1225086 699 / 699
1 aggressive 446 / 699 0.98% 9.2 h 1225086 699 / 699
``` ::: ::: ![Saturation detection across the 699-recording default pass: per-recording saturated-fraction distribution (left) and the 15 most-affected recordings with total saturated seconds labelled (right).](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_saturation_detection.png){.lightbox} 446/699 recordings (64%) have at least one detected saturated interval, totalling ~9.2 hours out of ~936 hours in the release (mean fraction 0.98%) — concentrated in a long tail of heavily-clipped insertions (up to 24% saturated) rather than spread evenly; most affected recordings lose well under 1% of their time. See the [saturation QC how-to](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/lfpack/how-to/bwm-dataset.html#saturation-qc) for how to query this per-recording via `LFPackReader.saturation` / `.saturation_summary` / `.saturation_mask`. **Labelling fix.** Every recording's saturation table now correctly reports `muted=True`. This required a fix, not just a rebuild: `compress_bin_to_h5` sets `muted = not checkpoint_existed` — an honest report of whether *this call* ran the mute step — which under-reports `False` whenever a build resumes from an already-muted Cadzow checkpoint (the normal case for this release, since decimation is checkpointed and expensive to redo). The v03 build's own checkpoints were already correctly muted, so the underlying data was never wrong — but the `muted` label was `False` for all 699 recordings until now. Fixed in two places: `sdsc-slurms/2026-06-lfpack/compress.py` now forces `muted=True` post-hoc for future reruns (the checkpoint-reuse guarantee is specific to that driver, so the fix lives there rather than in `lfpack` itself), and the existing v03 HDF5 attrs + QC parquet were patched in place. ## Release-wide QC (v03, all 699 recordings) ::: {#616bcf24 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
pass median RMSE (µV) RMSE > 25 µV median total CR
0 default 15.2 122 / 699 115
1 aggressive 25.1 352 / 699 308
``` ::: ::: ![Release-wide RMSE and compression-ratio distributions across all 699 BWM recordings, default vs aggressive pass. The dashed line marks the 25 µV design target.](figures/2026-07-24_bwm_release_qc_distributions.png){.lightbox} The default pass sits at median RMSE ≈15 µV / CR ≈115, consistent with the ε=150/α=28 operating point calibrated on the 11-PID benchmark in [index.qmd](index.qmd); 122/699 recordings (17%) exceed the 25 µV design target in the default pass — expected tail behaviour on genuinely low-SNR or high-saturation insertions, not a regression (RMSE ≤25 µV was a median target, not a per-recording guarantee). **Caveat:** the two fully-bad recordings above report `rmse_mean = 0`, which reads as suspiciously perfect — it reflects a degenerate all-bad-channel input reconstructing exactly, not compression quality, and should be excluded before aggregating RMSE across the release. A further 2 recordings (`30dfb8c6…`, `7441d0df…`) have `frac_bad` between 0.5–0.7 and should be treated with the same caution. ## Conclusion The v03 BWM release fixes the zero-damage codec bug across the full dataset with no regressions, ships a new saturation detection/muting pipeline stage with correctly-labelled metadata across all 699 recordings, and its release-wide RMSE/CR statistics are consistent with the benchmark calibration. Both compression passes (`lf_compressed_all_bwm.h5`, `lf_compressed_aggressive_all_bwm.h5`) were published to `s3://ibl-brain-wide-map-public/resources/ibl-agent-data/` on 2026-07-24, replacing v00.
